page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction sets including AVX-512, AES-NI, and VAES.

The hallmark of this server is its high memory-to-core ratio, delivering 504.0 GB of system memory, or 31.5 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage and includes no integrated GPUs, relying on attached network storage for disk operations. It also provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, adhering to standard private virtual network deployments.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent median-tier performance across compute and memory workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 8759.0, a single-core score of 1448.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 16593.6. Memory throughput reaches 695.21 GB/sec on small cached blocks and 99.79 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers, driving 13.12 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression and CPU-based LLM text generation fall into the lower performance quartile.

By constraining 16 vCPUs onto an underlying host footprint that typically supports 64 vCPUs, this server profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy applications subject to per-core commercial software licensing. Primary workload fits include large relational database engines, massive in-memory caching platforms, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial memory residency without high core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive workloads that require constrained CPU counts. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside an expansive 504.0 GB of memory, delivering 31.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance features no local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights solid median-tier capabilities, including 13.12 million Redis SET operations per second, a multi-core Geekbench score of 8759.0, and 99.79 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth, though CPU-driven LLM inference and single-threaded compression throughput remain modest. This constrained-core configuration maximizes cost efficiency for software environments licensed per core, making it well-suited for enterprise relational databases, large-scale caching layers, and in-memory analytics platforms.
